summary:
Cryptography lane on shop.lab.test (read-only). 

CRYP-01 (weak TLS) — DONE: There is no TLS at all. TCP connections to port 443 are refused ("Nothing answered at :443") while port 80 serves the full app over cleartext HTTP, with no HTTP->HTTPS redirect. This is the weakest possible transport posture. Recorded as a high lead.

CRYP-03 (sensitive info over unencrypted channel) — DONE: Over cleartext HTTP, the sign-in form posts credentials to http://shop.lab.test/login, the persistent session cookie (Max-Age=1yr, no Secure flag) is set/sent in the clear, and /static/app.js exposes an AWS access key id (plus a Stripe key) to the browser. All exposed to network interception. Recorded a medium lead for the AWS key in client JS.

CRYP-02 (padding oracle) — N/A: No client-controllable ciphertext exists. The session token is opaque and gateway-redacted (cannot be set to arbitrary values here) and no encrypted URL params/tokens are used; order and API data are plaintext JSON. A padding oracle cannot be exercised read-only.

CRYP-04 (weak encryption) — N/A: No application-level ciphertext or algorithm is observable to assess cipher strength; token values are redacted/opaque and app data is returned in plaintext. The only cryptographic weakness present is the total lack of transport encryption, captured under CRYP-01/03.

Note: cross-lane leads (missing cookie flags, BOLA/BFLA, logout CSRF, etc.) were already recorded by other lanes and are consistent with the HTTP-only finding here.
